newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - S&P adds to S. Korea's woes.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - S&P adds to S. Korea's woes.

text.p: Following Moody's Investors Service's review of South Korea, Standard & Poor weighed in on Wednesday with a warning that South Korea's outlook is negative.
S&P said on Wednesday it affirmed Korea's AA-minus long term foreign currency outlook, but changed the outlook to negative from stable.

"The negative outlook indicates the possibility of a downgrade as a result of the potential cost to the government of restructuring South Korea's troubled banking and corporate sectors, as well as the risks to its credit standing of North Korea's economic difficulties," it said.
Moody's said this week that it was reviewing Korea's Prime-1 foreign currency short term notes and bank deposit ratings, and A-1 foreign currency rating for long term bank deposits.
S&P last week put Thailand's long-term foreign currency and local currency ratings on review for possible downgrade, blaming greater-than-expected loan losses in the Thai financial sector.
The rash of reviews is dampening the debt market, sidelining those Korean and Thai issuers, who are not prepared to sweeten debt issues with higher yields or put options or "credit" clauses.
However, bankers said Thailand and Korea's loss is "Greater China's gain", with mainland, Hong Kong and Taiwan all being wooed by bankers.
"The focus is clearly on Hong Kong, China and...Taiwan," said one European banker, saying Chinese credits were looking better and better to lenders.
One banker working on the Hua Nan Commercial Bank US$100 million five year floating rate note (FRN) said the all-in in the "low 20s" (basis points) reflected keen interest in Taiwan.
"The pricing is tight, but the credit is good," he said.
The issue, Hua Nan Commercia's first offshore, is being launched through an offshore banking unit, and features a call option on the third anniversary.
Hua Nan Commercial is rated A2 by Moody's and is one of Taiwan's top three banks.
"Taiwan has not been too active in the international markets, (but) actually that might change," said one banker.
"We think there could be more (deals) coming," he added.
Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp is tipped to issue about HK$3.5 billion through a three year floating rate certificate of deposit (FRCD) issue.
Price talk points to an all-in of 27 basis points, the same as HongkongBank's three year FRCD in May, bankers said.

But one banker said HongkongBank had issued a lot of paper this year, and should sweeten its all-in yield. "I think the market's looking for something a little bit higher, probably closer to 30 (basis points)," he said.
Also borrowing is Lung Kee Metal Ltd, which is raising HK$200 million through a HK$200 million dual-tranche three-year deal (equally split between revolving credit and term loan).
All-in at top level is 139.54 basis points.
-- Sean Kennedy (852) 2847 4043
